approach: Add `crates/athena-core/src/slots.rs`: a lock-file counting semaphore of `max_check_slots` files under `<state root>/slots/`. Waiters register a ticket file that they hold locked until they are served or die. Only the head waiter, ordered by effective class, then enqueue time, may try the slot files. The exclusive file lock is the slot, so the OS frees it on drop or process death, and a ticket whose lock is free is dead. `SnapExec::exec` takes a `Class::Check` slot after `refuse_if_stopped` and the first-check disk gate. It holds the slot in a Drop guard through `run_check` and `restore_to`. It stamps the measured wait on the returned `CheckRun` as optional `queued_s`. A wait past `build_wait_s` returns a new `disk::SlotWait` error. `run/mod.rs` turns it into a resumable hold with reason `environment: build slot wait`, using the existing hold-and-resume path and no attempt. `PipelineConfig` gains `build_wait_s` (1800) and `build_age_promote_s` (600) with validation. `status.rs` prints a `build wait` line (sum of `queued_s`) in the throughput section. The Class order (landing, then check, then producer) and ageing live in slots.rs. Only `Class::Check` is used now.

decisions.choice: Counting semaphore from N lock files (`slot-0.lock`..`slot-{N-1}.lock`, exclusive `File::try_lock`). A fair queue is made of per-waiter ticket files under `slots/queue/`. Each ticket is created under a temp name, locked, then renamed into place, so a visible ticket with a free lock is always dead. Only the head ticket (lowest effective class, then earliest enqueue time, then name) tries the slots, and waiters poll (default 250 ms).
decisions.reason: This is the model design section 4 names: state.rs `lock_file`/`try_lock_job` use std `File::try_lock`, and the lock dies with the process, so a crash frees the slot with no sweeper. Tickets give strict class order, FIFO and ageing across the drain, `athena go` and (later) a shell. They need no daemon. Lock-then-rename removes the create-then-lock race.

rejected.option: Slot files only, with every waiter polling `try_lock` on each
rejected.why: This is unordered, so the 'first in first out inside a class' and class-order rules of section 4 could not hold.

rejected.option: A pid or heartbeat file with a sweeper
rejected.why: Section 4 and the acceptance criteria require that a crash frees the slot without a sweeper. Pid reuse and stale-file races add new failure modes.
It would not be shared between separate `athena` processes (drain, `go`, a producer shell), which is the point of the design.

rejected.option: A global single lock when max_check_slots = 1
rejected.why: It would not enforce counts above 1 and would need a second code path.

decisions.choice: The slot is acquired once per check in `SnapExec::exec` and dropped at the end of that call, after `restore_to`, through a plain `let slot = ...` guard. It is not held for the whole checks stage.
decisions.reason: The design says 'takes a slot per check', and 'one command that compiles or runs tests'. Drop covers every return path (`?` on `run_check`, `restore_to` error, panic).

rejected.option: Hold one slot across all checks of a job
rejected.why: The design's unit is one command, and it would starve other jobs for the whole fmt+clippy+test sequence.
This is easy to miss on an error path. Acceptance criterion 5 asks for Drop.

decisions.choice: Slot taken after the disk gate, as the accepted reading says, and before `run_check`.
decisions.reason: It matches the accepted reading and keeps the existing gate-once semantics (`gated` Cell) and the LowDisk tests unchanged.

rejected.option: Take the slot before the disk gate so free space is measured right before the build
rejected.why: It departs from the accepted reading. The verifier gate re-checks space after the checks anyway (`verification.rs:165`).

decisions.choice: The timeout hold is a new `disk::SlotWait { waited_s, limit_s }` error with `BUILD_SLOT_WAIT = "environment: build slot wait"`. Its marker goes in the same `hold_file` as `LowDisk` (distinct fields) through `write_slot_hold`/`read_slot_hold`. `hold_for_disk` is refactored to share one `commit_hold` helper. `read_hold`/`LowDisk` are unchanged.
decisions.reason: The records commit, the dispatched-with-no-process state, the resume mark and `clear_hold` are all reused, so the job is held and resumed with no attempt used. `LowDisk` has about a dozen test and call sites that compare it, so it is not widened. One marker file means `clear_hold` clears both kinds. `StopCause::of` already reads the text as `OtherEnvironment`, so the reason is an environment stop.

rejected.why: This would put false numbers and the text 'low disk' in the hold line and the marker.
It breaks every `downcast_ref::<LowDisk>` and `read_hold == Some(low)` test in athena-core and athena-cli.

rejected.option: Close the job failed with an environment reason
rejected.why: The design says held, not failed, using no attempt. A closed job would be an outcome.

decisions.choice: `queued_s: Option<f64>` on `CheckRun` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, set in `SnapExec::exec` from a monotonic `Instant` (basis 'athena monotonic clock'). The status 'build wait' line is added to `Throughput` as `build_wait: Option<BuildWait>` and printed only when some check has a `queued_s`.
decisions.reason: The brief wants the field on each check in verification.json with old records still reading. Printing the line only when data exists leaves every existing throughput text assertion unchanged. The producer must add `queued_s: None` to every `CheckRun { .. }` literal (found by grepping `revert_for:`), which the compiler enforces.

rejected.option: A separate new record file type for slot waits
rejected.why: Out of scope. The reading says no new record file type.

rejected.option: Always print the line, with zero when none
rejected.why: This changes the output for repositories with no data and risks existing text assertions for no gain.

decisions.choice: The `acquire` loop takes a `stop: &dyn Fn() -> Result<()>` closure (`Athena::refuse_if_stopped`) and calls it every poll.
decisions.reason: A wait can last up to 1800 s, and the kill switch (`athena stop`) must still end it. Today `exec` checks the switch before every check.

rejected.option: Check the kill switch only before the wait
rejected.why: A stopped job would sit in the queue for up to build_wait_s.

risks.risk: A cross-process ticket race: a ticket that is visible but not yet locked reads as dead and is removed, so a live waiter loses its place.
risks.mitigation: The ticket is created under a temp name, locked, then renamed into place (flock follows the inode), so a visible ticket with a free lock is always dead. The unit tests include a dead-ticket case.

risks.risk: Polling latency (250 ms) or head-of-line waiting slows contended runs. When 2 or more slots are free, only the head tries.
risks.mitigation: A limit of 1 is today's behavior and an uncontended `acquire` returns at once, with the ticket served on the first iteration. The poll interval is a field. Waiters behind the head are served within one poll after each release.

risks.risk: Changing `CheckRun` forces edits in about 12 files outside the deliverable list.
risks.mitigation: Every edit is the mechanical `queued_s: None`. The compiler flags any missed literal, and `grep revert_for:` lists them. The file list names them all.

risks.risk: Existing tests that assert the whole throughput text or the exact hold text could break.
risks.mitigation: The 'build wait' line is printed only when some check has `queued_s`. `read_hold` and `LowDisk` are unchanged. The full `cargo test --locked` is the criterion 8 demonstration.

risks.risk: Tests that use real processes and sleeps are flaky: the re-exec'd child holder, and the 1 s `build_wait_s` wait.
risks.mitigation: The child prints a marker the parent waits for before asserting, so there is no sleep-based race. Waits are asserted as lower bounds ('at least 0.3 s'), never exact. The 1 s limit is the smallest valid value, since the key is whole seconds.

risks.risk: The disk gate runs once, before the first slot wait, so free space may be stale by the time a queued job runs its build.
risks.mitigation: This follows the accepted reading. The verifier gate re-checks space after the checks. Recorded in the design note; no change to gate placement.

risks.risk: A job holds a slot while its check runs up to `check_timeout_s` (1800), equal to `build_wait_s`. A waiter can then time out behind one slow check, producing a hold.
risks.mitigation: This is the designed bound (section 4). A hold resumes by itself on the next drain pass and uses no attempt.

risks.risk: `File::try_lock` on a read-only or missing state directory fails.
risks.mitigation: `acquire` creates `slots/` and its files as `state.rs::lock_file` does. An I/O error is a normal error with context, not a hold.

demonstrations.method: A full-job test in run/tests.rs plus a slots.rs unit test with two threads. In the full-job test, a helper thread acquires the only slot through `SlotQueue::acquire(Class::Check)` on a clone of `athena.state` (same production call `SnapExec` makes) and signals ready. The main thread then runs `Athena::go` for a job whose check is faked by the existing `check_seam`. The helper holds about 500 ms, appends 'released' to a shared log, and drops the slot. The seam closure appends 'ran' to the same log.
demonstrations.observes: The log reads released, then ran, so the second job did not run while the slot was held. `verification.json` of the landed job has `queued_s` of at least 0.3 on its check. The slots.rs two-thread test shows the same order for two `acquire` calls on one state dir.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the slot in `SnapExec::exec`, 'ran' is logged before 'released' and `queued_s` is None, so both assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Athena::go` -> `SnapExec::exec` -> `SlotQueue::acquire`. Fake: the existing thread-local `check_seam::install` (`run/mod.rs:1194`) supplies the `CheckRun`; the repository is `repo_with_config("")`, so the limit is the default 1. `athena_with` (`run/tests.rs:183`) builds the Athena over a tempdir state. The holder is the real `SlotQueue` on a cloned `StateDir` (Send). `StateDir` clone and the seam exist today. `SlotQueue` is added by step 2.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in slots.rs that re-executes the test binary (`std::env::current_exe`, args `--exact slots::tests::slot_holder_child --nocapture`, with an env var naming the slot dir and a marker) as a child. The child test acquires a slot, prints HELD and sleeps. The parent reads HELD and asserts a non-blocking `try_acquire` on the same dir fails with the child alive. It then kills the child (`Child::kill`, SIGKILL) and `wait`s, and a blocking `acquire` succeeds with no cleanup call. A second test panics in a thread that holds a `Slot`, and the waiter acquires after the unwind.
demonstrations.observes: While the child lives the slot is refused. After SIGKILL the waiter gets the slot within a poll or two with no file removed, which proves that a held lock, not a file's existence, is the slot. The panic variant also frees the slot.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the slot were a created/removed file or a pid file with no sweeper, the waiter would time out after the kill and the test would fail. If the slot did not exclude, the pre-kill refusal assertion would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `SlotQueue::acquire` and `try_acquire` on a tempdir `slots_dir`. The seam is the real child process, in the same environment (root) as production, so no mock holds the lock. The child test body is gated by an env var so a normal run returns at once. `SlotQueue::new` takes the dir and limits explicitly. Step 2 adds `SlotQueue` and its `new(dir, slots, wait, promote)` constructor; `StateDir::slots_dir` is added by step 1.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in slots.rs with `max_check_slots` = 2 and three threads calling `acquire` on one dir. A shared `AtomicUsize` counts live holders and records the peak. The test also calls `try_acquire` while two are held, then releases one.
demonstrations.observes: Peak concurrent holders is 2, never 3. The third request returns only after a release, with queued time above zero. `try_acquire` while two are held is refused and succeeds after one drop. Separate tests cover class order, FIFO and ageing: a Check waiter queued later overtakes an earlier Producer waiter, equal classes go first in first out, and a Producer waiter older than `build_age_promote_s` is promoted past a Check.
demonstrations.fails_without: A limit of 1 or no limit fails the peak == 2 or the 'third waits' assertion. Missing ordering fails the class tests.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `SlotQueue::acquire`/`try_acquire` with real threads and tempdir lock files. There is no double. The poll interval is a `with_poll` builder option (default 250 ms) set small in tests. Both are added by step 2.

build_wait_s = 1
")`. A test-held `Slot` from the production `SlotQueue` keeps the only slot for the whole first `go`. Then `go` is called and its error is checked. After the holder drops, `athena.retry` and `go` finish the job.
demonstrations.observes: `go` returns an error that downcasts to `disk::SlotWait`. The ui has a line starting `held       environment: build slot wait`. The job is `JobState::Dispatched` with no outcome, no score and no verification. `read_slot_hold` returns Some, and `read_hold` (the LowDisk reader) returns None. `is_environment_reason(&text)` is true. The producer count is 1 and the verifier count is 0. After release the retry resumes with no producer rerun and lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the SlotWait hold, the wait would never time out, or the timeout would surface as a plain error or a failed outcome. The Dispatched/no-outcome/no-attempt assertions and the downcast fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Athena::go` -> `SnapExec::exec` -> `SlotQueue::acquire` -> `Athena::hold_for_slot_wait`. Fixtures: `repo_with_config` (exists, `run/tests.rs:291`), `athena_with`, `counting` and `plenty_of_space`. The holder is the real `SlotQueue`. `build_wait_s` reaches the code through the committed athena.toml via `JobConfig`, as `check_timeout_s` does. No test clock is needed (1 s real). Step 6 adds the config keys and step 4 the hold.

demonstrations.method: A test that the guard drops on the error path, plus listing the file. The test makes `SnapExec::exec` return early after the slot is taken (the disk gate returning LowDisk, via the existing `low_once_built`-style free-space fake, or a failing `restore_to`), then calls `SlotQueue::try_acquire` on the job's state and expects success. `ls` shows slots.rs.
demonstrations.observes: slots.rs exists. After a `go` that returned early, the single slot is free at once, so the guard is released by Drop on that return path. After a normal run it is free too. The verifier can also read `SnapExec::exec` to see the guard bound before `run_check` and living past `restore_to`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the guard were leaked (`mem::forget`) or released only on the success path, `try_acquire` would be refused after the early return.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go`. Fixture: the existing free-space fakes in `test_support.rs` (`low_once_*`, `plenty_of_space`) injected through `athena_with`. All exist today. The assertion helper is `SlotQueue::try_acquire` from step 2.

demonstrations.method: Config tests in config.rs: defaults give 1800 and 600, explicit values parse, a zero for either key is refused naming the key, and an unknown key under `[drain.pipeline]` is still refused. The existing `bad_drain_pipeline_settings_are_refused_naming_the_key` list gains `build_wait_s = 0` and `build_age_promote_s = 0` next to the unchanged `surprise = 1`. `drain_pipeline_defaults_keep_todays_behavior` also asserts the new defaults. `reading_inputs_ignore_a_non_default_drain_pipeline` keeps passing, so the config digest stays unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: The default tuple includes (1800, 600). The zero keys give `ConfigError::DrainPipeline("build_wait_s")` etc. `surprise` is still refused. The digest and reading-inputs equality hold.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new fields the defaults assertion does not compile or fail. Without validation the zero cases parse OK and the `expect_err` fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Config::parse` with the `REPO_CONFIG` fixture (exists in config.rs tests). There is no double. `PipelineConfig` stays `Copy`, so the new fields are `u64`.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. In records.rs, a `CheckRun` JSON without `queued_s` deserializes with None and re-serializes without the key. One with `queued_s: 12.5` round-trips, and the AnyRecord verification tests still pass. In status.rs, a test builds landed jobs whose verification checks carry `queued_s` of 12.0 and 30.0 plus a reused check with None, then calls `Throughput::compute(...).text()`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-data records:: && cargo test -p athena-core status::tests::the_throughput_section_sums_build_wait
demonstrations.observes: The old JSON reads. The text contains a line starting `build wait` with the total 42 s, the count of waited checks, and the basis 'athena monotonic clock'. With no `queued_s` anywhere, the text has no such line, so existing throughput text assertions are unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, the old-record test is trivial but the new-field round-trip fails to compile or fail. Without the status summation the line is absent and the contains assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `AnyRecord::parse`, serde on `CheckRun`, and `Throughput::compute`/`text` over `Records` built by the existing `loaded(...)`, `timed_job` and `test_run` helpers in status.rs tests (`status.rs:2888`, `3279`). No double. Step 5 adds the field and the line.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks. This works because the default `max_check_slots` is 1 and the queue is uncontended in every existing test, and because every `CheckRun` literal across crates is updated.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. No existing test changes behavior, including the LowDisk hold tests, the drain tests, and status and records tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing `queued_s: None` literal fails compilation. A slot that blocked at limit 1 even when uncontended would hang or fail the existing job tests.
demonstrations.seam: These are the production commands Athena runs on the result. Every existing test already runs with the default `max_check_slots` of 1 through `Athena::go`. State dirs are tempdirs, so the slot files are isolated per test.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff: nothing under athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github, or records/, and an entry in CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased > Added.
demonstrations.command: git diff --stat -- athena.toml defaults.toml .github records && git diff -- CHANGELOG.md
demonstrations.observes: The first command prints nothing. The second shows a new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` describing the build-slot queue, the two config keys, the `build slot wait` hold and `queued_s` with the 'build wait' line.
demonstrations.fails_without: A forgotten changelog shows an empty diff for CHANGELOG.md. An accidental governance edit shows in the first diff.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion, so there is no seam. It is a content check on the repository diff.

open_questions: User: Should the baseline check run and the 'fails without' reruns (`take_baseline`/`baseline_checks`, `demonstration_runs` in run/checks.rs) also take a build slot in this step? The request and reading name only `SnapExec::exec` (local checks) and the design lists 'reruns' among the askers, but they have no hold path today and are not in the acceptance criteria. The plan leaves them unwrapped.

User: Should ageing promote a waiting request by one class once (at `build_age_promote_s`) or by one class per interval? Section 4 says 'moves up one class'. The plan promotes one class per interval waited, capped at class 1, so a long wait cannot starve. Only one class is used in this step, so nothing observable depends on it yet.
